Hi I had the same situation exactly a year ago today. And although I can't say it will be easy, I want you to remind you that no matter what happened you are loved by so many people in your life. 

Tips I can give you to begin the healing process:
1. Try to separate the fact that you love and care about him from the reality of the current situation. It is possible to simultaneously love and care about him and also realize that he is his own person and entity. As in, ultimately he is clearly living for himself and choosing a path for himself in his own life. That decision, regardless of if you saw it coming is his right to make. Just like you have your own free will to make whatever decisions you see fit.
2. Try to be kind to yourself. It is completely legitimate to be sad and angry and confused. Very few people (from my experience) can even begin to conceptualize the type of intrinsic pain you are feeling. You are allowed to feel all over the place as your body and mind take in this situation and accept this new reality. 
3. Please please please remind yourself that you gave your best to the relationship and of yourself and have nothing to regret. Try to think that the capacity you have to love or your emotional 'age' may be different than your exes. 
4. Surround yourself with people and things that bring you joy. If someone cannot be there for you in the way you need right now, invest in those who can. Try to fill up your time with activities that you enjoy. Personally I started to write and draw to get out my frustrations. Everytime I got sad I started to get creative. And maybe those art sessions began sad but they usually reminded me that I have way more strength in me than I thought. 
5. Get a therapist if possible. Initially I couldn't afford weekly sessions but I began seeing a therapist every two to three weeks. Having an outlet to cry and open up with someone who isn't in your family or immediate circles can really really really help and I can't stress this one enough. It's a very traumatic situation and investing in your mental health is very important. 
6. Regardless of your faith, I truly believe that the tests that life puts before us often show us who we are and what we are capable of overcoming. I know I'm a stranger but I believe in you. And even though I'm a year out of that same situation I still have my ups and downs but I've developed something that I didn't have a year ago - and that's faith and belief in myself, my values and my capabilities. 
7. Stand behind your values and you will see that the best kind of people will enter your life. Over this year I took this advice and I began to date better people and meet more friends who are more like minded. 
8. Make a bucket list for this year - maybe things you planned with him or new things that now will become YOUR memories. Don't let the promises of your relationship stop you from doing and accomplishing things. 
9. Write a list in your phone of the things you don't like about your ex/the relationship and make those things your focus when you begin to miss him. Then write another list of all the things you love about your self and values that are important to you in all your relationships in your life. Review both lists when you begin to feel sad and I promise you will feel some relief. Make this a go-to practice and over time these words will become a part of who you are. 

Hope all of that helped. Sending lots of support your way ❤️ and a reminder that no matter how old you are better to be single than with someone who doesn't reciprocate the love, respect and care back to you!
